package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2017-9805) due to improper handling of XML payloads in the XStreamHandler class, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code via malicious XML documents.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when REST plugin is enabled and XML payload is processed)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: public Object createXStream() { ... // improper XML deserialization with XStream ... }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deserializes attacker-supplied XML payloads using XStream without proper validation, allowing arbitrary code execution if a malicious XML document is provided.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted XML data without validation is a well-known vector for remote code execution attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would require strict validation or whitelisting of XML types before deserialization. The actual behavior allows arbitrary object instantiation from attacker-controlled input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate XML deserialization is common in REST APIs, but only with trusted sources and strict type controls.
key_indicators: Use of XStream without type whitelisting
Known CVE (CVE-2017-9805) affecting this code path

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted malicious XML payload to a REST endpoint using the vulnerable plugin.
attack_chain.leads_to: XML payload is processed by the vulnerable XStreamHandler.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable createXStream method deserializes the XML without validation, instantiating attacker-controlled objects.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution on the server (RCE).

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted XML data at runtime
Use of XStream library without type whitelisting
Processing of attacker-supplied XML in REST endpoints
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with XML payloads to REST endpoints
Unusual outbound connections from the application server after XML processing
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for use of vulnerable Struts2 REST plugin versions (<=2.5.12), especially when the XStreamHandler class is present. Inspect application logs for errors or stack traces involving XStream deserialization. Use network monitoring to detect suspicious inbound XML payloads and unexpected outbound connections following XML processing. Employ static analysis to flag unvalidated XStream deserialization code paths.
